title: Subnuclear genome compartmentalization controls bivalent chromatin activity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read GEO file lists for GSE274038 (one 17 GB RAW tar holding ~120 bigWig signal tracks of 30-340 MB each plus small BED domain calls) and GSE274039 (8 bulk RNA-seq TPM files from cell-line neural progenitors and neurons). Downloaded and opened 4 domain BEDs: GW17 radial glia has 345 LADs (lamina-associated domains) covering 1.28 Gb, GW17 excitatory neurons 794 LADs; speckle-associated domains (SPADs): 740 in radial glia, 612 in neurons, with a score column. One H3K27me3 peak file has 49,357 peaks; one TPM file has 60,719 Ensembl genes. A ranged read of one lamina bigWig returned a valid bigWig header, so remote range reads work. GitHub repo holds analysis scripts only, no tables.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Assay details (GO-CaRT, a CUT&RUN-based method, against LMNB1 and SON), the three cell types (radial glia, intermediate progenitors, excitatory neurons) sorted from GW16-20 cortex, the 'hundreds of relocating genes' and eightfold expression change. Raw reads are controlled access in dbGaP phs000989; fetal cortex expression sits in the NeMO archive (not opened). I did not open any bigWig body, so per-bin values, normalisation and replicate agreement are unverified; the paper's LAD/SPAD counts were not compared with the BEDs.

a1_downloadable.note: Processed bigWigs and BEDs download from GEO with no login (checked file lists and fetched BEDs). Raw reads are controlled access in dbGaP, but the project doesn't need them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Label = lamina or speckle signal (log2 ratio over an IgG antibody control) per genomic window, read out of one bigWig per sample by fixed-window averaging. No joining across sources needed, but no ready table exists: every label must be binned out of the tracks first.

a3_inputs_present.note: Input is the hg38 reference DNA sequence at given coordinates, plus histone tracks from the same series. Coordinates checked in the BEDs; the genome build is assumed hg38 from the paper, not stated in the files.

a4_units_stated.note: File names state 'scaled.log2' ratio over IgG for lamina/speckle tracks and RPGC (reads per genomic content) for histone coverage. Units are implied by file names, not by a units column.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 30,000 windows of 100 kb across the genome per sample (my estimate, not counted from files). The independent units are much fewer, though: 345-794 domains per cell type (checked in BEDs), all from one lab.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~4.5 GB of raw bigWigs for 18 lamina/speckle tracks (GEO sizes); <50 MB after binning
a6_fits_laptop.note: Each bigWig exceeds the 50 MB download cap, but remote ranged reads (pyBigWig-style) let you bin without downloading the whole file. Header read verified.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not cross-checked: paper's domain counts not extracted. Files are internally consistent (replicate pairs present for each cell type and mark).

a8_label_provenance.note: Per-window signal is a direct sequencing measurement. The LAD/SPAD BEDs are outputs of a domain caller (an HMM-based caller, and SEACR, a peak caller), so use the raw signal rather than the calls.

B1.why: ~120 separate bigWig tracks plus BEDs; no window-by-feature table exists (seen in GEO file list).

B2.why: BEDs parsed first try; bigWigs need a reader library and binning code, not plain csv.

B3.why: Tracks are scaled log2 over IgG per sample; cross-sample comparability across donors needs checking (paper text, not verified).

B4.why: Continuous signal, no censored values; only unmappable windows need masking.

B5.why: One track per sample/replicate; no duplicated measurements beyond intentional replicates.

B6.why: File names encode cell type, week, mark and replicate; normalisation described only in paper methods.

C1.why: Transfer question (do sequence features predict cell-type-specific relocation?) is informative, but the per-window task means beating existing models.

C2.why: Nucleotide GPT was fine-tuned on this exact GW17 cortex data; LADDER and UNADON exist; code and splits unclear.

C3.why: Weak angle: cell-type-resolved relocation in fetal cortex over neurogenesis, which LADDER (cell-type independent) ignores.

C4.why: GO-CaRT on sorted fetal cortex cells is rare, costly tissue work; a predictor would substitute.

C5.why: Nucleotide GPT reports 73.6% LAD / 79.4% SPAD accuracy, split unspecified; GC/gene-density baseline obvious.

D1.why: DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer and HyenaDNA are open-weight DNA models.

D2.why: Embedding ~3 Gb of sequence on CPU is many hours; feasible only with small windows or subsampling.

D3.why: Mixed: DNABERT-2 Apache-2.0; Nucleotide Transformer CC BY-NC-SA.

E1.why: Hold out whole chromosomes; chromosome is in every BED/bigWig row.

E2.why: 22 autosomes give many held-out groups; donors only 2-3 (GW16, GW17, GW20 in names).

E3.why: GC content and gene density per window are trivial, known-strong baselines.

E4.why: Two replicates per cell type and mark in GEO file list give replicate correlation.

E5.why: Lamina signal must anticorrelate with GC/gene density and with speckle signal (textbook).

E6.why: Label shuffling within chromosomes and feature-block ablation are straightforward.

E7.why: Public lamina/speckle maps in cell lines (4DN TSA-seq, DamID; Kind LAD atlas) offer external tests.

E8.why: Nucleotide GPT code/weights and split not found; its numbers can't be reproduced as is.

G1.why: Genomic coordinates in BEDs; TPM file uses versioned Ensembl gene IDs (checked).

G2.why: 4DN Data Portal lamina DamID / SON TSA-seq in H1, K562, HFF, HCT116, joinable on hg38 coordinates.

G3.why: Fixed genomic windows join one-to-one across resources once build is fixed.

G4.why: Combined question: is nuclear position mostly sequence-encoded or cell-type-specific? Partly asked already by UNADON.

H1.why: Genome-wide signal covers associated and non-associated regions alike.

H2.why: One lab, 2-3 fetal donors, one tissue.

H4.why: Donor count and gestational weeks visible in file names; tissue limits partly documented.

I1.why: 3D-genome and neurodevelopment labs (e.g. Lim lab, UCSF; Ma lab, CMU) broadly.

I2.why: Could prioritise genes for relocation experiments, but marginal over existing maps.

I3.why: Per-window correlation roughly matches 'is this gene at the lamina in neurons?'.

I4.why: GC/repeat density already explains much lamina association; ML adds some.

J1.why: Heavy signal processing before modelling; DNA language-model embeddings are real ML.

J2.why: Textbook LAD/GC relationships give sanity checks; chromatin biology needs expertise.

J3.why: Binned multi-track table is shareable; model result may be marginal.

existing_models.name: Nucleotide GPT (bioRxiv 2024.11.27.625761), a DNA transformer fine-tuned to classify LADs/SPADs
existing_models.score_and_split: 73.6% average LAD accuracy, 79.4% SPAD accuracy across GW17 radial glia, progenitors and neurons, 8 kb windows; split not specified.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: 8 kb window misses long-range dependencies; cell-type-specific factors beyond sequence modulate association during differentiation.

existing_models.name: LADDER (Patterns 2026), multimodal deep model on sequence plus gene/LINE1/SINE density
existing_models.score_and_split: Held-out chromosome 15 test, chromosome 11 validation, 512 kb windows; strong Pearson/ROC-AUC reported (exact numbers not retrieved). Cell-type independent.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cell-type-specific lamina patterns not captured; weak on chromosomes with little lamina association.

existing_models.name: UNADON (arXiv 2304.13230), transformer predicting SON and LMNB TSA-seq from sequence and epigenomic features
existing_models.score_and_split: Cell lines K562, H1, HCT116, HFFc6; cross-cell-type evaluation; exact numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: SPIN (Genome Biology 2021), hidden Markov random field combining TSA-seq, DamID and Hi-C into nuclear states
existing_models.score_and_split: Unsupervised state caller in K562, not a predictor.

backbone.name: DNABERT-2 (open DNA language model) or HyenaDNA-small, frozen embeddings averaged per window
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible only on subsampled windows; full-genome embedding wants a GPU
backbone.licence: DNABERT-2 Apache-2.0; Nucleotide Transformer CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

integration.partner_dataset: 4DN Data Portal lamina DamID and SON TSA-seq maps in H1, K562, HFF and HCT116 cell lines
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: How much of a genome region's position at the lamina or speckle is fixed by its DNA sequence, and how much is rewritten cell-type-specifically during human cortical neurogenesis?

controls.positive_control: Lamina signal anticorrelates with GC content, gene density and speckle signal; a model must recover this.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within chromosomes; replace sequence embeddings with GC-matched random sequence.
controls.external_validation: 4DN cell-line DamID/TSA-seq maps and the Kind et al. LAD atlas; second donor (GW20) as a held-out donor.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts lamina and speckle association of 100 kb genome windows in three sorted neural cell types from 2-3 mid-gestation fetal cortex donors profiled by one lab with GO-CaRT, tested on held-out chromosomes.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence of a genome region to predict whether it sits at the nuclear edge or near speckles in developing human brain cells.
plain_idea.train_on: About 30,000 genome windows of 100 kb (an estimate; not counted from the files), each with its DNA sequence and histone marks, in three brain cell types.
plain_idea.predict: How strongly each window contacts the nuclear lamina (the nucleus's inner edge) or nuclear speckles, measured by antibody-targeted cutting and sequencing (GO-CaRT) on cells sorted from fetal cortex.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would tell neurodevelopment labs whether a gene's move from the nuclear edge to speckles during neuron birth is written in its sequence or set by the cell type.

more_or_better_data.why: Nucleotide GPT already used this lab's GW17 cortex data; ours adds GW20, H3K9me2 and continuous signal, but covers the same 3 cell types. LADDER used 4 non-brain-specific cell types.

confidence_score.why: Two replicates per track allow a per-window noise estimate; none of the named models report calibrated uncertainty, as far as retrieved.

models_beatable.why: Nucleotide GPT (2024 preprint) uses 8 kb windows and an unspecified split; LADDER (2026) uses an honest held-out chromosome but is cell-type independent, so cell-type-specific prediction is open.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model is runnable as a baseline (no code or weights found), and partner 4DN data comes from other cell types and assays (DamID, TSA-seq), so it doesn't measure the same quantity in the same way.

label_elsewhere.sources: 4DN Data Portal (lamina DamID, SON TSA-seq in several cell lines; known resource), Kind et al. LAD atlas (known resource), van Steensel lab DamID datasets.
label_elsewhere.why: Cell-line lamina/speckle maps let a model trained on brain cells be tested on unrelated cell types, separating sequence-encoded from cell-type-specific positioning.

risks: Neighbouring windows inside the same multi-megabase LAD share both sequence features and label, so a random split leaks through spatial autocorrelation.
Replicates and donors of the same cell type are near-copies; splitting them across train and test inflates scores.
LAD/SPAD calls are derived from the signal itself, so using calls of one mark as features for the other is near-circular.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes (chromosome column present in every BED row, seen); additionally hold out the GW20 donor for a donor-transfer test (donor in file names, seen).
checks: Shuffle labels within chromosome and confirm collapse to the GC-content baseline.
Train on GC content plus gene density alone and report how much the sequence model adds.
Report performance as a function of distance to the nearest training chromosome region (should be flat under chromosome holdout).
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable with chromosome holdout; spatial autocorrelation is the main trap.

success_criteria.metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and measured per-window change in lamina signal from radial glia to neurons on held-out chromosomes, because the open question is cell-type-specific relocation.
success_criteria.baselines: GC content plus gene density linear model (to compute); Nucleotide GPT 73.6% LAD accuracy (split unspecified, not directly comparable).
success_criteria.success: Spearman on held-out chromosomes for the radial-glia-to-neuron change at least 0.1 above the GC/gene-density baseline (threshold set by me, no published number on this split).
success_criteria.kill: If the sequence model adds under 0.05 Spearman over GC plus gene density for the relocation target after one week, stop.

ambitious.why: Publishes 3D-genome method papers; would need clear evidence that sequence predicts cell-type-specific relocation beyond GC content, validated in a held-out donor.

realistic.why: Fits a modest benchmark showing how much sequence explains of fetal-brain nuclear positioning versus simple baselines.

fallback.why: A negative result (sequence adds nothing over GC for relocation) is still a short, citable note.

pitch.headline: Rare paired lamina and speckle maps for three sorted neural cell types from fetal human cortex, at two gestational weeks, with replicates.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Sorted primary fetal cortex cells, not cell lines: 345 versus 794 LADs in radial glia versus neurons (checked in BEDs), plus matched H3K27me3, H3K4me3, H3K9me2 and Pol II tracks.
pitch.the_win: Sequence model beats a GC/gene-density baseline by at least 0.1 Spearman at predicting which windows leave the lamina from radial glia to neurons, on held-out chromosomes.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Quantifies that cell-type relocation during neurogenesis is not sequence-encoded, which supports the paper's claim that position is set by cell state.
pitch.who_wants_it: Lim lab (UCSF, authors) and 3D-genome modellers (Ma lab, CMU; LADDER authors) deciding whether sequence-only nuclear-position models suffice for development.

ml_idea: Bin GO-CaRT lamina (LMNB1) and speckle (SON) bigWigs into 100 kb windows for radial glia, progenitors and neurons; predict per-window signal and radial-glia-to-neuron change from frozen DNA language-model embeddings plus GC/repeat density, with chromosome holdout and GW20 donor holdout; test transfer to 4DN cell-line maps.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, nothing timed: binning 18 bigWigs via ranged reads is I/O-bound; a GC/repeat baseline on ~30k windows takes minutes; full-genome language-model embedding on CPU is impractical, so embedding cost depends on subsampling and is left null.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Bin one radial-glia and one neuron lamina bigWig at 100 kb and fit GC content plus gene density: if that already explains most of the change in lamina signal between the two cell types on held-out chromosomes, there's nothing left for a model.

verdict_reason: Part A passes, but the data is ~120 genome-wide signal tracks rather than a table (B scores 7 of 12), a 17 GB genomics resource, and Nucleotide GPT was already fine-tuned on this lab's same cortex data. Worth revisiting only for the cell-type relocation transfer question.
